message.content: {"output_action": "CREATE", "skill_draft": {"name": "differentiate_nodule_distribution_patterns", "description": "When interpreting pulmonary nodules on CT, distinguish between random, centrilobular, and perilymphatic distributions to avoid misdiagnosis.", "applicable_conditions": "Applicable to any chest CT interpretation task involving multiple pulmonary nodules where the differential diagnosis depends on nodule distribution patterns.", "branch": "task_level", "tool_name": null, "task_category": ["medical_imaging_interpretation"], "required_tools": [], "risk_level": "high", "core_action": "When analyzing pulmonary nodules on CT: (1) Check for involvement of subpleural lines and fissures; if present, classify as perilymphatic (suggesting sarcoidosis or lymphangitic carcinomatosis). (2) If nodules spare the immediate subpleural lung and fissures but cluster around bronchioles, classify as centrilobular (suggesting hypersensitivity pneumonitis or endobronchial spread). (3) If nodules are uniformly distributed without regard to anatomical structures, classify as random/miliary (suggesting miliary TB or hematogenous metastasis). Do not default to peribronchovascular without confirming fissural involvement."}, "patch_target_id": null, "patch_section": null, "patch_content": null}
